checks: No eclipse at 3 of 119 covered epochs where the 1.29654 d period predicts one (each under half the typical depth, > 5 sigma below it). The period is probably wrong - the dips seen may be separate eclipses of a longer-period system.
writeup: TIC 42011712 is a candidate eclipsing binary star system identified through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The system shows a primary eclipse with a depth of 1.25 percent occurring every 1.2965 days, while no secondary eclipse was detected. The eclipse signal achieves a detection significance of 80.6 in the box-least-squares periodogram analysis. Pixel-level difference imaging confirms the signal's presence near the target location, with a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 20.5, though the centroid offset of 2.3 arcsec warrants consideration. The candidate does not appear in any of six major variable-star catalogs, making it potentially novel. The machine-learning screening model assigned this candidate a score of 0.18, reflecting moderate confidence that this represents a genuine target star rather than instrumental noise or background contamination.
